'''Virender K. Sharma''' is an American chemist whose research focuses on ferrate chemistry, water science and technology, and environmental engineering. He is a professor of professional practice at the [[University of Miami]] College of Engineering. His work centers on the development and application of high-valent iron compounds, particularly ferrate (Fe(VI)), for water treatment, environmental remediation, and public health protection..<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=TWRI |date=2020-10-09 |title=Meet a scientist: Virender Sharma |url=https://twri.tamu.edu/blog/2020/10/09/meet-a-scientist-virender-sharma/ |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=Texas Water Resources Institute |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= Virender K. Sharma|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=p4viQtkAAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Sharma |first=Virender K. |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781118482469 |title=Oxidation of Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins |date=2012-11-30 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-470-62776-1 |language=en |doi=10.1002/9781118482469}}</ref>

==Education==

Sharma earned a Bachelor of Science in chemistry (1980) and a Master of Science in chemistry (1982) from the [[University of Delhi]].<ref name=":2"/> He sebsequently completed a Master of Technology (1984) from the Indian Institute of Technology. In 1989, he received his Ph.D.<ref name=":2" /><ref name="GS">{{Cite web |title=Virender K. Sharma |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8T0KE7EAAAAJ&hl=en |website=Google Scholar |access-date=2025-09-23 }}</ref> in marine and atmospheric chemistry from the Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science at the University of Miami.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Virender Sharma |url=https://people.miami.edu/profile/f585741b0eca714518175bb1ced20b52 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=people.miami.edu |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==

Following completion of his doctoral studies,Sharma held a postdoctoral fellowship at the State University of New York at Buffalo (1990–1991), where he also lectured at [[Millard Fillmore College]].<ref name=":2" /> He later worked at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and held visiting positions at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] and [[Drury College]].<ref name=":2" />

From 1992 to 1999, he was a faculty member at Texas A&M University–Corpus Christi. He then joined the [[Florida Institute of Technology]] (1999–2013), where he directed the Center of Ferrate Excellence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sharma |first=Virender K. |date=2002-03-01 |title=Potassium ferrate(VI): an environmentally friendly oxidant |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1093019101001198 |journal=Advances in Environmental Research |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=143–156 |doi=10.1016/S1093-0191(01)00119-8 |bibcode=2002AdvER...6..143S |issn=1093-0191|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2014, Sharma joined [[Texas A&M University]], where he became a professor in the School of Public Health and director of its Program of the Environment and Sustainability.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharma |first1=Virender K. |last2=Feng |first2=Mingbao |last3=Dionysiou |first3=Dionysios D. |last4=Zhou |first4=Hong-Cai |last5=Jinadatha |first5=Chetan |last6=Manoli |first6=Kyriakos |last7=Smith |first7=Mallory F. |last8=Luque |first8=Rafael |last9=Ma |first9=Xingmao |last10=Huang |first10=Ching-Hua |date=2022-01-04 |title=Reactive High-Valent Iron Intermediates in Enhancing Treatment of Water by Ferrate |journal=Environmental Science & Technology |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=30–47 |doi=10.1021/acs.est.1c04616 |issn=1520-5851 |pmid=34918915 |bibcode=2022EnST...56...30S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar Citations |url=https://accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier?continue=https%3A%2F%2Fscholar.google.com%2Fcitations%3Fview_op%3Dsearch_authors%26hl%3Den%26mauthors%3Dlabel%3Aenvironmental_chemistry&dsh=S-1660507078%3A1758653281365340&hl=en&ifkv=AfYwgwVeaDdK8_l6s3ja0tofwOBWHlBeyUSiETfuf1Uuqc1RbYkj7kyk-DItoHoxqxh5xN2qfCawyA&service=citations&flowName=GlifWebSignIn&flowEntry=ServiceLogin |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=accounts.google.com}}</ref>

In 2025, Sharma joined the University of Miami College of Engineering as a professor of professional practice.<ref name=":0" />

He has also held visiting research appointments at the University of Paris-Est, Palacký University in the Czech Republic, the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], and [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":2" />

==Research==

Sharma is known for his contributions to the chemistry and application of ferrate compounds in water and wastewater treatment. His research has examined the mechanisms of ferrate oxidation and the development of processes for producing stable liquid ferrate solutions. These advances have supported applications in drinking water treatment, pathogen inactivation, pollutant degradation, and control of disinfection byproducts.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharma |first1=Virender K. |last2=Zboril |first2=Radek |last3=Varma |first3=Rajender S. |date=2015-02-17 |title=Ferrates: Greener Oxidants with Multimodal Action in Water Treatment Technologies |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |volume=48 |issue=2 |pages=182–191 |doi=10.1021/ar5004219 |pmid=25668700 |issn=0001-4842}}</ref><ref name="GS" />

His studies have addressed contaminants including pharmaceuticals, antibiotic-resistant bacteria, arsenic, nanoparticles, and microplastics.<ref>{{Cite patent|number=US8961921B2|title=Apparatus and method for producing liquid ferrate|gdate=2015-02-24|invent1=Sharma|inventor1-first=Virender K.|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US8961921B2/en}}</ref><ref name="GS"/> According to Expertscape, he has been ranked among leading experts globally in research related to water pollutants.<ref>{{Cite patent|number=US20120091040A1|title=Method and Apparatus For Desulfurization of Heavy Oil Using a Ferrate(VI)|gdate=2012-04-19|invent1=Sharma|invent2=Al-Abduly|inventor1-first=Virender K.|inventor2-first=Abdullah|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US20120091040A1/en}}</ref>

Clayton |last3=Nesnas |first3=Nasri |last4=Lee |first4=Yunho |last5=Huang |first5=Ching-Hua |last6=Sharma |first6=Virender K. |date=2019-03-05 |title=Oxidation of Sulfonamide Antibiotics of Six-Membered Heterocyclic Moiety by Ferrate(VI): Kinetics and Mechanistic Insight into SO2 Extrusion |journal=Environmental Science & Technology |volume=53 |issue=5 |pages=2695–2704 |doi=10.1021/acs.est.8b06535 |issn=1520-5851 |pmid=30715861 |bibcode=2019EnST...53.2695F }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Schnettler |first=Tim |date=2021-08-23 |title=Sharma receives National Science Foundation grant - Vital Record |url=https://vitalrecord.tamhsc.edu/sharma-receives-national-science-foundation-grant/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240227055614/https://vitalrecord.tamhsc.edu/sharma-receives-national-science-foundation-grant/ |archive-date=2024-02-27 |access-date=2025-09-23 |work=Vital Record |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The top 10 causes of death |url=https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/the-top-10-causes-of-death |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.who.int |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharma |first1=Virender K. |last2=Ma |first2=Xingmao |last3=Lichtfouse |first3=Eric |last4=Robert |first4=Didier |date=2023-08-01 |title=Nanoplastics are potentially more dangerous than microplastics |journal=Environmental Chemistry Letters |language=en |volume=21 |issue=4 |pages=1933–1936 |doi=10.1007/s10311-022-01539-1 |bibcode=2023EnvCL..21.1933S |issn=1610-3661}}</ref>He is the author of ''Oxidation of Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins: Kinetics and Mechanism'' (Wiley, 2001) and has edited volumes in environmental chemistry and water research.

<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Water Pollutants: Worldwide - Expertscape.com |url=https://expertscape.com/ex/water+pollutants |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210828162938/https://expertscape.com/ex/water+pollutants |archive-date=2021-08-28 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=expertscape.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Patents'''

He holds seven patents related to ferrate production methods and water treatment technologies, including processes for generating liquid ferrate and applications in disinfection and pollutant removal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Rae Lynn |date=2023-05-08 |title=School of Public Health professor receives patent for effective, environmentally friendly surface disinfectant |url=https://vitalrecord.tamu.edu/school-of-public-health-professor-issued-fifth-patent-since-joining-texas-am/ |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=Vital Record |language=en-US}}</ref>
